lesson: In flagcore's bucket(), the hash input must strictly be user_id + ":" + flag_name encoded as UTF-8 bytes before running crc32.
why: Analytics recomputes this exact CRC32 string to attribute events, so the bytes must match as an interface contract, and simple concatenation without a separator causes collisions.
quote: The hash input is pinned: user_id + ":" + flag_name, colon separator, exactly that string. Analytics recomputes the same crc32 on their side

lesson: In flagcore's bucket(), use a counter metric by (flag, in/out) alongside a debug endpoint instead of logging every bucketing decision.
why: The bucket() function runs on every request, so full logging would overwhelm and crash the log collector.
quote: Sampled metric, not logs - bucket() runs on every request and full logging would melt the collector

lesson: In flagcore's bucket(), compare the bucket value against percent using strict less-than (bucket < percent), rejecting less-than-or-equal (<=).
why: Using <= causes bucket 0 (approx. 1% of traffic) to remain enrolled even when percent is set to 0, preventing experiments from ever being truly disabled.
quote: Strict less-than, and this one matters more than it looks: bucket < percent. With buckets 0..99, percent=0 must enroll NOBODY

lesson: In flagcore's bucket(), corp accounts (ending in @corp.example) must only be force-enrolled if the flag name begins with the prefix beta-.
why: A blanket corporate override allows internal flags to unintentionally leak to external or shared demo accounts.
quote: Corp accounts - user ids ending @corp.example - are always in ONLY when the flag name starts with beta-.

lesson: The corp-beta override check in flagcore's bucket() must be evaluated first before any percent or hashing logic.
why: Evaluating it first allows teams to create a beta flag at 0% rollout for internal dogfooding before rolling out to general users.
quote: The corp-beta override is absolute and evaluated first - a beta- flag at 0% still shows for every corp account

lesson: Deploy the hash input update in flagcore as a single cutover with no legacy dual-hash path.
why: Maintaining a legacy hash path would preserve cross-flag cohort correlation bugs for existing flags indefinitely.
quote: No dual-hash - we take the one-time churn. Running experiments restart their measurement window after the deploy

lesson: Do not clamp or re-validate the percent value inside flagcore's bucket().
why: Percent values are already validated (0..100) at write time by the flag store, and clamping inside bucket() would obscure upstream store bugs.
quote: the flag store validates percent at write time, so assume 0..100 and don't clamp - a clamp would hide store bugs.
